commits.message:
refactor(markup): pair plugin tags and style tags in one walk (rich-markup-pyq5) (#277)

* refactor(markup): pair plugin tags and style tags in one walk (rich-markup-pyq5)

renderMarkup read each slice's tags twice: pairPluginTags kept its own copy
of the open-tag stack to find plugin pairs, crossings and overlaps, and
render walked the same tags again to build spans. The two had to agree on
every closing rule by hand, and did not.

Now one walk over the whole string holds one stack and one rule for what a
closing tag names (namedBy). A plugin tag's content is written into a frame
of its own; when the tag pairs, the frame is the handler's children, and
when it never does, the frame folds back where it stood and the tag is a
style span over it. The slice recursion, SliceOrigin, MarkupPart, within()
and the pairing pass are gone.

Behaviour changes, each pinned in markup-plugins.test.ts:
- Rejections come out in string order: '[/x] [red][aa]x[/red][/aa]' now
  reports the stray [/x] at column 1, not the crossing at column 16.
- A style tag's closer cannot reach past an open plugin tag, even one that
  later turns out never to close. Deciding that at the closer is what makes
  string order possible; the old rule needed to know whether the plugin tag
  would pair.
- '[/]' that reaches past a pair's end to a plugin tag is reported as an
  overlap of the two plugin tags, not as a style crossing.

* fix(markup): one output buffer, so an unclosed plugin tag costs a style tag (rich-markup-pyq5)

Folding each unpaired plugin tag's content frame into its parent on close was
quadratic in nesting depth. The walk now writes into one buffer; a pair takes
its content off the tail, and an unpaired tag is only a span.

A closer names a tag by style name or by plugin name, and ends a pair only for
[/] or its plugin's own name, so [aa]x[/aa=x] closes [aa] as a style tag again.

* fix(markup): a crossing's reason names a plugin tag, not a pair it may never form (rich-markup-pyq5)
